description: Real public iPhone backups used by the corpus tests (layer L1 in docs/BACKUP_TEST_CORPUS_PLAN.md). None of them are stored in this repository: `python -m corpus.fetch` downloads them into a local cache. Passwords are listed only where the creator published them.

items.creator: Joshua Hickman
items.terms: Free for training, education, testing or research (creator). Link to the creator's blog post, not the files. Do not download cloud data from apps in the image. Not for redistribution or screenshots.
items.notes: Same phone as pub-hickman-13.4.1 and pub-hickman-14.3. The archive also holds a full-file-system extraction of the same phone (layer L2 calibration pair). SHA-256 pinned on first fetch (2026-10-10): the creator's PDF publishes no hash for the backup zip, and the member passed the archive's own CRC check.

fetch.instructions: The backup is the folder 'Users/eliflatt/Library/Application Support/MobileSync/Backup/518e8d766f9b3e76db216f35fdb6b0604e50f61b/' (2,135 files, about 153 MB) inside https://digitalcorpora.s3.amazonaws.com/corpora/scenarios/magnet/2021%20CTF%20-%20MacOS.zip (81 GB, stored entries). Copy that folder out (range requests or a full download), zip it with the UDID folder at the top level, and name the zip as shown. The backup password is in the keychain export '..._passwords.txt' (service 'BackupAgent') inside '2021 CTF - iOS.zip' in the same folder; put it in this item's 'password' field once confirmed.

fetch.instructions: Download 'CTF21_Marsha_PC_Physical_DC' (5-part zip, about 44 GB) from the Google Drive folder linked on Cellebrite's CTF 2021 pages. The zip password is in Cellebrite's ZIP_Password.txt. Mount 'sda Image.E01' (libewf / ewfmount), copy 'C:\Users\marsh\Apple\MobileSync\Backup\efa74738...\' out, and zip it with the UDID folder at the top level.
